chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him): In

a man pays another man thirty dirhams for one garment and twenty dirhams for another, so he sends back both garments but does not know which is which. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The two garments are sold, and the owner of the thirty receives three-fifths of the price, and the other receives two-fifths of the price.' I said: 'If the owner of the twenty says to the owner of the thirty, choose whichever you wish,' he said: 'He has treated him fairly.'

key_terms.أَنْصَفَهُ: He treated him fairly / He gave him his due right
key_terms.يُبْضِعُهُ: He pays him / He gives him a sum of money

ai.seo_question: How is debt or mixed payment settled when the specific items cannot be distinguished?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of evidences, this hadith illustrates the Shia juristic principle of proportional distribution (nisab) when specific assets become indistinguishable due to a debtor's action. The Imam’s ruling validates a 3:2 split based on original debt values, while also acknowledging that mutual consent to a random selection by the creditor constitutes a valid, fair settlement (insāf), highlighting the flexibility between strict legal entitlement and equitable agreement.
